summary: UEFI NVRAM boot-entry exhaustion causes SCCM imaging task sequence to loop on Lenovo X13 during depot reimage
description:
Issue summary: Several Lenovo X13 units fail to complete the SCCM task sequence during depot reimage. The TS halts at the 'Apply OS' phase and then the machine reboots back into PXE/WinPE repeatedly (imaging loop).

Impact: Blocks depot reimage throughput for a small batch (7/120) of Lenovo X13 devices; delays fleet refresh and repair turnaround. Not customer-facing but affects internal device provisioning SLA.

Background: Devices were returned from a test group where engineering had temporarily enabled multiple boot profiles and experimented with dual-boot UEFI entries. Those machines are now hitting imaging failures.

Observed behavior: SCCM task sequence fails to locate boot manager after the first reboot post-OS apply and re-enters WinPE. Devices show >200 UEFI boot entries in NVRAM and the firmware reports NVRAM storage near capacity, causing firmware to drop newly written Boot#### entries used by the TS to continue.

Expected behavior: NVRAM should accept the Boot#### entries SCCM creates during TS and allow the system to continue the normal reboot path into the newly applied OS.

Workaround in place: Manual NVRAM cleanup via vendor utility before imaging succeeds; we have a stopgap script run by depot techs that clears non-essential Boot#### entries prior to TS but this is manual and slow.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Take a Lenovo X13 with >= 150 existing UEFI Boot#### entries (e.g., after repeated dev dual-boot changes).
2) Boot to PXE and start SCCM task sequence (depot reimage).
3) SCCM applies OS image and writes Boot#### entry for Windows Boot Manager.
4) On first reboot, firmware reports NVRAM write failure silently and drops the new Boot####, leaving system without a valid boot path; device returns to WinPE PXE.

Observed in 7 devices across two depot batches; reproducible on 1 lab unit after intentionally flooding NVRAM with entries.
logs:
UEFI log snippet from FW debug console (device 13-03-26):
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] NVRAM capacity: 96% (used 512k / 536k)
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] CreateBootEntry(LoaderPath=\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi) -> status=0x80 (NVRAM_STORAGE_EXHAUSTED)
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] WriteVariable(Boot0001) -> dropped, no space
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] FirmwareFallback: continue to PXE

SCCM TS log (SMSTS.log):
Content of SMSTS.log around reboot: 14:22:20 Failed to create boot entry for OS; error 0x80070005
14:22:20 Marked step as failed, restarting 
14:22:30 System reboot to WinPE
investigation_notes:
Initial triage: Support reproduced failure in lab by creating >150 Boot#### entries via efibootmgr. Confirmed firmware reports 'storage exhausted' and silently fails to persist new entries.

Hypotheses considered:
- SCCM TS is correct; firmware NVRAM exhaustion is root cause.
- A firmware bug on X13 variants causes NVRAM to report capacity incorrectly when many entries exist.
- AssetDB or imaging scripts writing persistent entries in odd formats contributing to fragmentation.

Actions taken so far:
- Imaging eng ran lab repro and captured EFI variables (efivar -l) and vendor firmware debug logs.
- Opened vendor ticket with Lenovo @ case LEN-20260310-UEFI (attached logs).
- Created temporary depot script (scripts/cleanup_nvram.sh) that removes non-Microsoft Boot#### entries older than 30 days prior to running TS. Deployed to depot-ops as manual step.
- Proposed SCCM TS change: insert a pre-OS step to run NVRAM cleanup from WinPE using efibootmgr-equivalent vendor utility. PR created: https://github.com/redwood/it-imaging/pull/614

Remaining unknowns:
- Whether firmware will accept new entries after cleanup on all affected units or if some hardware requires firmware update.
- Whether repeated manual cleanup will result in NVRAM fragmentation that still blocks entry creation.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Kai Becker (Imaging Eng): Reproduced in lab by creating 180 efivars; confirmed firmware returns storage exhausted. Captured efivar output and vendor debug logs.
2026-03-11 08:37 - Priya Singh (Depot Ops): Deployed manual cleanup script to depot-ops. Three units imaged successfully after manual cleanup. Depot throughput improved but process is slow.
2026-03-11 15:21 - Lenovo Support (via case LEN-20260310-UEFI): Acknowledged as firmware behavior; recommended BIOS update to 1.35 and provided vendor tool to compact NVRAM.
resolution_notes:
Short term: Continue manual cleanup script as mandatory pre-TS step for affected Lenovo X13 units. Depot ops trained and script added to runbook (confluence link).

Medium term: Merge PR to SCCM TS to perform automated NVRAM cleanup in WinPE before OS apply (PR 614). Rollout of TS change scheduled for 2026-03-18 to depot pool; will run in canary on 5 devices.

Long term: Lenovo provided BIOS firmware 1.35 addressing NVRAM handling. Plan coordinated with hardware lifecycle to push firmware update to depot (BIOS package QA scheduled 2026-03-20). After firmware rollout, we will monitor for recurrence and remove forced cleanup step.

Follow-ups:
- Add telemetry to imaging pipeline to record current efivar count and NVRAM capacity after TS completes.
- Run a sweep of returned/dev units to compact NVRAM ahead of reprovisioning where possible.

Ticket will be closed after successful canary and firmware rollout with no recurrence for 7 days.
priority_notes: P2 chosen because this affects internal SLAs and depot throughput but does not affect production customer workloads.
